title: Assessing the clinical utility of composite outcomes in studies examining outcomes of implantable neuromodulation therapies for pain: a systematic review
authors: Olivia Soyoung Chung; Gretchen Mae Gabriel; Abeer Alomari; Anuj Bhatia
pain_condition_detail: Chronic refractory pain of moderate-to-severe intensity treated with implantable neuromodulation therapies; includes neuropathy, vascular aetiologies, complex regional pain syndrome, and other causes.
context_note: Country of origin will be extracted; no broader cultural, geographic, or healthcare-system context is otherwise stated.
bps_function_set: justification; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: It operationalizes BPS as a measurement architecture: extracted outcomes include pain intensity, physical health, mental health, quality of life, medication use, and explantation/failure rates, with pain intensity used as comparator. It does not define the model, specify causal pathways, or analyze social determinants.
integration_mechanism_summary: None proposed. The paper links domains by arguing that unidimensional pain intensity and eligibility thresholds miss physical, mental, social, quality-of-life, medication, and explantation outcomes; composite measures are proposed as a measurement architecture, not a causal pathway.
pain_conditions_1: chronic refractory pain of moderate-to-severe intensity
quality_assessment_tools_4: begg’s rank test / egger’s regression test
bps_model_variants_2: complex biopsychosocial nature of chronic pain
conceptual_tensions_1: BPS is invoked to justify multidimensional assessment, but no definition, causal pathway, or social mechanism is provided
conceptual_tensions_2: Pain intensity is criticized as insufficient yet remains the eligibility threshold and comparator outcome
conceptual_tensions_3: Composite outcomes are proposed as a solution, but the paper states no standardized composite outcome currently exists
conceptual_tensions_4: Patient satisfaction is described as important but is not clearly represented in the planned extraction domains
conceptual_tensions_5: Social function and social well-being are named, but extraction focuses on pain, physical health, mental health, quality of life, medication use, and explantation
additional_observations_1: This is a protocol, all study conduct and synthesis are future-tense
additional_observations_2: It will extract demographics and country of origin but not social determinants, family, culture, or healthcare access
additional_observations_3: It will standardize pain intensity to a 0–10 scale for comparison
additional_observations_4: It proposes meta-analysis with RevMan and Forest plots, but no BPS model is modelled statistically
additional_observations_5: The BPS frame is measurement-oriented rather than explanatory
synthesis_note: This protocol uses BPS mainly as a justification for composite outcome measures in implantable neuromodulation studies. It names pain intensity, physical health, mental health, quality of life, medication use, and explantation outcomes, with only brief social references. No BPS definition, causal pathway, or social mechanism is proposed; the model is operationalized as a measurement checklist.
coding_rationale: BPS is explicit but undefined. Biological/intervention content is dominant; psychological and social content are named as outcomes only. No cross-domain mechanisms are proposed, supporting pseudo-BPS.

title: Assessing the clinical utility of composite outcomes in studies examining outcomes of implantable neuromodulation therapies for pain: a systematic review
authors: Olivia Soyoung Chung; Gretchen Mae Gabriel; Abeer Alomari; Anuj Bhatia
pain_condition_detail: implantable neuromodulation therapies for refractory pain
bps_operationalization_summary: Organizes outcome domains (physical health, mental well-being, social function) as components of composite measures without defining or integrating the biopsychosocial model as a theoretical framework.
conceptual_tensions_1: Tension between using pain intensity as sole eligibility criterion versus the need for multi-domain assessment

additional_observations_2: Psychological constructs are operationalized through specific instruments while biological and social domains remain conceptual
synthesis_note: This systematic review examines composite outcomes for implantable neuromodulation therapies, identifying a gap between unidimensional pain intensity measures and the need for multi-domain assessment. It uses BPS language to frame the problem but does not integrate the three domains conceptually. Psychological constructs are well-defined through instruments, while biological and social aspects remain underdeveloped. The review is psychologically dominant and multifactorial in typology, with no triadic integration proposed.
coding_rationale: BPS typology is multifactorial because all three domains are mentioned but not integrated. Psychological domain is elaborated through specific instruments. No triadic integration exists as domains are treated as parallel rather than interconnected.

Eligibility for these therapies remains heavily reliant on unidimensional pain scale scores, which do not fully capture the complex biopsychosocial nature of chronic pain.
key_quotes_03_why_it_matters: Explicitly identifies the gap in standardized composite outcomes for neuromodulation therapies
